title: Pongal, the harvest
hookLine: a Tamil harvest festival thanking the sun and the cattle; the rice pot boils over for luck
last: THEY THAT SOW IN TEARS SHALL REAP IN JOY.

lines: A NEW POT FACING THE SUN.
cards: Early morning in a courtyard in Tamil Nadu. A pattern of rice flour, a kolam, has been drawn on the ground outside the door.
A new clay pot sits over a fire, facing the rising sun, with turmeric leaves tied around its neck. Inside: new rice, milk, and jaggery. The whole family is watching it.
Nobody is stirring. They're waiting for the moment it rises to the rim and spills over the side. When it does, they shout.

teach.b: First, the name. Pongal is both the festival and the sweet rice dish cooked for it. Tamils keep it as the month of Thai begins, when the harvest is in, and it runs over several days.
The main day thanks the sun, Surya, for the harvest. The pot is set out in the open, facing east, and the first rice of the new crop is cooked and offered before it's eaten.
The meal begins with thanks to the light the fields depend on. Third, the cattle. A day is set aside for the cows and bullocks that pulled the plows.

They're washed, their horns are painted, they're hung with bells and flowers, and they're fed some of the sweet rice. The animals who did the work get thanked like workers, because they were. Fourth, the overflow.
Tradition says the pot boiling over is a good sign, a picture of a household where good things spill beyond the rim.
People call out Pongalo Pongal as it rises. Usually a pot boiling over is a mess to clean up. Here, it's the whole point.
The Tamil classic, the Thirukkural, has a chapter in praise of farming. In paraphrase, one of its couplets says that however far the world wanders, it still follows the plow.
Pongal is the day the world turns around and thanks the plow, the sun and the ox, and lets the pot run over.

how: At Pongal, Tamil families draw kolam patterns at the door, cook new rice with milk and jaggery in a new pot facing the sun until it boils over, call out "Pongalo Pongal", and honor their cattle on a day of their own.

games.q: you're at the pot. the milk and rice are rising fast toward the rim. what do you do?
o: turn down the fire before it spills.
wait, and shout when it boils over.
games.why: the spill is the point. tradition says the overflow is a good sign for the house.

practice: Picture the pot on the fire, the milk rising slowly, the family waiting, and think of one good thing in your life sitting just under the rim: a thank-you not yet said, a compliment kept to yourself, some time or food you could share.
Let it rise in your mind, and picture where it might spill over, and to whom. If you pray, you can give thanks in your own tradition's words for whatever feeds you.

wordCard.voice: Pongal. The Tamil harvest festival and its sweet rice, cooked until it boils over, with thanks to the sun and the cattle. Today's word.
